shared_limits: This is not blanket old/new Python API compatibility. Retired module names, constructors and saved active schemas are identified separately from current user workflows.

Historical reader/ASR/Studio/provider/assistant declarations retain exact passive provenance. Restore/import does not grant execution, external path, source quotation, credential, device or output-replacement authority.

Canonical historical ASR retention accepts 32 GiB per source and 64 GiB aggregate inputs. Current library-wide new execution remains separately bounded to 32 GiB aggregate. Generic backup state and metadata have their own limits. No actual 64 GiB throughput measurement is claimed.

The real Dordiai owner-specific adapter is distinct from the generic local helper. Warm-worker reuse/performance, private model inference, multilingual/acoustic quality and physical audio/NVDA remain unqualified.
Current DSP output/sample rates/cache identities are not relabelled as identical old artifacts. Optional named procedural SFX is absent; required reviewed Sound/Clip functionality is present.
Current passive generated backup does not reproduce the entire canonical generated graph validator. Its existing envelope/byte checks and current consumer hard refusal are separately recorded.
Current Gyan runtime acquisition and old BtbN provisioning have different binary/source/license provenance. This audit grants no corresponding-source or redistribution clearance.
One mandatory visible Studio form action remains open at this document boundary. The canonical semantic merge must reference its actual reviewed repair, not assume script access is equivalent.

Generated-backup observed fixture repair only. It preserves the existing backup envelope so current consumer validation is actually reached; no producer product behavior changes.
